37.notes: The solution states as fact: "So the power falls to a quarter of its first value. The option wording means reduced to a quarter." This claim about what the wording means is false. "Reduced by a quarter" and "reduced to a quarter" are not the same thing: reducing a value BY a quarter (25%) leaves three-quarters of it, it does not leave a quarter of it. They only happen to coincide for the special case of one-half (reduced by half = reduced to half), which is likely why the author generalised the pattern here, but it does not hold for a quarter. The physics working (power falls to 1/4 = a drop of 3/4) is correct, but asserting that 'reduced by a quarter' literally means 'reduced to a quarter' teaches a false equivalence a student could carry into the next question, e.g. wrongly reading 'reduced by a third' as 'reduced to a third'.
37.fix: So the power falls to a quarter of its first value, a drop of three-quarters. Read the option's wording carefully: reducing something BY a quarter would normally leave three-quarters of it, but here 'reduced by a quarter' is used to mean the power ends up as a quarter of its start value, so treat it as 'reduced to a quarter' for this option.

Using the stem exactly as printed (mass 0.0025 kg, v = 250 m/s), p = mv = 0.625 kg m/s and lambda = h / p = 6.67e-34 / 0.625 = 1.07e-33 m, one power of ten above option C's printed 1.07e-34 m. The digits 1.07 match no option except C, so C correctly stays the key, and the solution is transparent about the mismatch rather than hiding it, so it does not mislead the student. I agree the likely source of the error is the stem's mass: 0.025 kg (not 0.0025 kg) gives p = 6.25 kg m/s and lambda = 6.67e-34 / 6.25 = 1.07e-34 m, matching option C exactly.
